# ✋ Read this first

- **What this does:** you write a short movie on one node (who is in it, where it happens, and every shot), make a picture for each person and place, and press **Run**. It renders the shots one after another with MiniMax H3 and joins them into one movie with sound and dialogue.
- **Do the steps in order.** Every step uses what the step before it made. Skipping ahead is the fastest way to get strangers in random rooms.
- **💡 The guided tour:** open **Vision Assistant** (the left sidebar) → **Tour**. It lights up each part of the workflow in order and marks the settings that matter. Use it alongside this note.
- 🛑🚫 **Don't bypass nodes by hand.** **Cards & Storyboard 🃏** is bypassed on the inside on purpose. The **✨** buttons switch on what they need and put it back.
- ⚠️ This is a **long job** on a **big model**. 32 GB of VRAM is comfortable at 960 x 544. Less works, just slower.

## The basics
- **This workflow saves every step.** 
   - If you create images, video sections, etc., you can 💾 save the project, work on a different project, and come back to it or redo a section at any time.
   -  **Nothing is lost:** what finished stays finished.
- **Pictures and the movie are separate Runs:**
    - **Pictures:** press **✨** on a card's picture slot (steps 2 and 3). The Story switches on the part of **Cards & Storyboard 🃏** that makes it, keeps **Make 🎥** off, runs once and puts everything back.
    - **Movie:** press **Run** (step 4). **Make** renders every shot that isn't made yet.
    - ⚠️ **Make has to be off while a picture is made.** A new picture changes the shots that use it, and Make would render them again on the same Run. ✨ does that for you.
- **Save💾** Everything is saved in a **project** folder named on the Story node. Close ComfyUI, come back tomorrow, and it's all still there.

**🎨Post processing**
- Leave these switches off until you are ready to use it
- It processes the entire movie all at once and it is heavy, so I would not let it just run.
- Keep **Make 🎥** on (don't bypass it).

---

## ⚙️ Settings

- **megapixels**: 0.82 = 1216 x 672 (16:9). 0.52 (960 x 544) is faster, but faces in wide shots get very small.
   - Keep one size for the whole project. Change it anyway and the next Run makes every shot made at the old size again, in order (the 📐 size line lists them).
   - 💡 Don't stress too much over quality here. Push out decent, but 1 MP just slows down what you can upscale in the end.
- **Steps**: 12 with the turbo LoRA at 0.7 (the **Stock int8 + turbo LoRA 0.7** row in **Optimal setups and times ⏱️**). 8 with turbo at 1.0 is faster and a little softer. No turbo is slower and not better in my tests.
- **LC Seed**: the seed generator is the starting seed for H3 (each new shot) and the storyboard (MOSS and Krea 2: seed + shot number).
   - Every made shot keeps its own seed with its take, and ↻ (remake) always picks a new one.
   - The card pictures and post processing have their own seeds. Leave it alone.
- **Models & LoRAs**: the LC Optimizer picks the H3 files for your card. 
   - I suggest leaving it on **★ Recommended**.
   - I've tested it on other models. 10EROS works well, Singularity has voice issues. 
   - LoRAs. Your mileage will vary. 
- **Storyboard creator Models & Settings**: the models that make the pictures.
   - **Card Model (Krea2)** with the **Character or Style LoRA** makes the cast, outfit, place and prop pictures, and redraws the storyboard frames with the **🪪 Edit LoRA**.
   - **Storyboard model 📖 (MOSS)** lays the shots out from your boxes.
   - Leave both on **★ Recommended** unless you have your own.


---

## Step 1: 🎬 Write the story

Everything happens on the big **LC H3 Story** node. It has five lists: **🎭 Cast**, **👗 Outfits**, **📍 Places**, **👜 Props** and **🎞 Shots**.

- ✋ **The H3 prompt shows the shot's lines.** Make wraps the people, pictures and sound around them when the shot is made. Open a shot's **H3 prompt** to read it.
    - **↻** builds it again right now, so you see what will be sent before you spend time rendering.
    - **✎ Edit** lets you write it yourself. Your text is sent as written, and the cards stop changing it until you press **↶ Back to automatic**.
- **project name** (top): the folder everything is saved in, `output/LC_H3/<name>/`. Name it first. **📂** opens a saved project, **💾** saves now (every Run saves too). **💾 Save as** keeps a variant under a new name: the made shots come along and the original stays as it is.
- **📐 size** (under the project name): the size this project is made at (the last Run), with its aspect ratio. Shots made at another size are listed (⚠) and made again on the next Run.
- **The look of the whole movie** (top line): a few words for the film style ("cinematic, soft natural light, shallow depth of field"). It goes into every shot.

### 🖼 Picture slots
- Cast, outfit, place, 🌐 360, prop, 🖼 start and 🏁 end all work the same way.
    - Click a slot or drop a picture on it. **📚 Library** has ready-made ones, **⬆ Upload…** takes a file.
    - **✨** makes one for you (steps 2 and 3).
    - **↶** brings back the picture before this one. The last 8 are kept.
    - **✂** crops what the card uses of a picture (a head and shoulders out of a full-length photo, just the coat of an outfit).
    - **×** empties the slot (**↻** on a start or end frame).

### ✨ Write the story (optional)
- Type a short pitch ("Nova and Anika meet for coffee, Anika tells a story that goes too far, Nova leaves") and press **✨ Write the story**. A local model fills in the look, cast, places and shots once.
- After that it's plain text you edit. It never writes again unless you press the button again (which replaces the cards; pictures and voices on cards with the same name stay).
- Needs the **Story writer model** above. Pick it in the dropdown next to the button.
- **🔞 NSFW** (in the ✨ Write box, off by default): lets the writer write adult scenes, the same rule as LC Vision's NSFW style tag. Off, it writes the way it always has. Saved with the project.


### 🎭 Cast: one card per person
- **Name**: start with a capital letter. Shots find people by this exact name.
- **who**: woman, man, girl, boy, person, cat, dog. It tells people apart in the prompt.
- **look**: one line, the words H3 follows most. Describe the head and hair, then stop: age, face, eyes, freckles, skin, hair (length too). "mid twenties, a soft oval face, green eyes, light freckles, long wavy blonde hair". Never clothes: they go in the outfit picture.
    - ⚠️ No body words either (breasts, curvy, figure). Next to a bare-shouldered headshot they can make H3 leave the clothes off. The Story warns you (👗). The outfit picture shows the body.
- **face picture**: a headshot, made in step 2 (✨ on the slot), or yours (click the square or drop a picture on it). The background is automatically removed and the face is placed on a plain grey background to prevent it from bleeding into the scene or outfit.
    - Headshot means head and hair. No shoulders, no clothes: clothes in a headshot beat every outfit picture.
- **👗 outfit picture**: what they wear from their first shot, head to toe. Made in step 2 (✨ on the 👗 slot), or yours.
    - **outfit notes**: the whole outfit in detail. The picture is made from it, and H3 reads only its first piece of clothing as the outfit's name ("dark blue jumpsuit"). Start with the main piece and its color.
- **🎤 voice** (optional): a 2 to 15 s clip of how they sound. H3 copies the voice, not the words.
- **📋** copies the name and look to paste into another workflow.

### 👗 Outfits: the clothes, one card per outfit
- ✋ **Everyone needs clothes from somewhere.** The headshot carries none. Give each person a 👗 outfit picture on their cast card. With none, they get different clothes in every shot, and the Story warns you (👗).
- An outfit card is a change of clothes.
    - It can also be a state of dress: "naked", "topless, black jeans", "wrapped in a white towel". H3 gets it as written.
- **name**: a simple name: "red cocktail dress", "yoga outfit", "gym clothes". With a picture, it's all H3 reads about the outfit.
    - Never a list of pieces. Shoes and pants in the words pull close-ups wide (the Story warns you).
- **who wears it**: the person.
- **description**: the whole outfit head to toe, in detail, **a color for every item**, with the shade: "an off the shoulder grey cutoff sweatshirt, high waisted black leggings with a cross stitch band, white Nike gym shoes". Only the picture is made from it.
    - Layers outside first, with "over". Patterns name their colors ("floral blouse in pale peach and green"). Fabric helps (denim, silk, knit, leather).
- **picture**: made in step 2 (✨ on the slot: the person who wears it, head to toe, on plain grey), or yours. It carries every detail the name doesn't say.
- **How it plays:**
    - Everyone starts in their cast card's 👗 outfit. To change, pick another on a shot with **👗**, or name it in the action ("Nova comes back in the red dress"). They stay in it from that shot on.
    - Each shot gets "wearing <name>" in the prompt and the outfit picture. Close-ups stay close: no pants or shoes in the words.
    - Tested: a one-strap red dress with silver details came through from the picture alone, named just "red dress".
    - ⚠️ **Mismatched reference**: a cut back to an earlier camera opens on that shot's first frame, and a wide takes its room from the place's first wide. If that frame shows other clothes, people or props, the Story warns you. Pin a start frame, or give the scene its own place card.

### 📍 Places: one card per location
- **name**: "the cafe". Shots pick their place by this name.
- **sound**: sounds you can hear, nothing else: "rain on the glass, cups clinking, footsteps".
    - ✋ **Never write who speaks** ("nobody speaks", "no voices"). Naming speech makes H3 speak: the same silent shot talked in French and English with it and was silent without it. The Story adds "Nobody speaks." to a shot with no line by itself.
- **description**: what is there: the room, the furniture, the light.
- **room picture**: the place, **empty**. Made in step 2 (✨ on the slot), or yours.
- **🌐 360** (recommended): **one** panorama of the whole room (step 2, ✨ on the 🌐 slot). You don't make a picture per shot: the Story cuts each shot's view out of it by itself.
    - **Set it once:** turn the small viewer under the place until it shows what your wide shot shows (**📷 the wide shot faces**). That is "front". Every angle counts from there: 90 = right side of the room, -90 = left, 180 = behind the camera.
    - **Close-ups and medium shots get their view automatically.** One across the table from someone who already has an angle gets the reverse angle (+180), so the two of them have opposite sides of the room behind them. The others face the way the wide shot faces.
    - **Want a different angle?** Press **🌐** on the shot card and drag the view. Your angle always wins over the automatic one.
    - The view is cut as a flat picture (in the project's `views/` folder) and used as that shot's background, by Make and by the storyboard.
    - Wide shots use the room picture and the anchor, unless you aim them with 🌐 too.
- **📌 anchors**: frames that keep this room the same across cuts. Empty at first: see **📌 Anchors** below.

### 👜 Props: one card per object that matters
- Only for an object that must look the same in every shot (the red umbrella, the letter, the ring).
- **name**: "the red umbrella". ✋ Use these **exact words** in a shot's action, and that shot gets the prop's picture.
- **description**: what it looks like.
- **picture**: made in step 2 (✨ on the slot), or yours. It goes on plain grey like the cast.


**💡 Need something simple?** 
- Every cast, outfit, prop and 🌐 360 slot has a 📚 Library tab in its picture picker: 102 ready-made pictures (30 cast headshots, 32 seasonal outfits, 24 props, 16 360 panoramas). Browse them all: [LC H3 Library on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lonecatone23/lc-h3-library)


### 🎞 Shots: one card per shot, top to bottom is the movie
- **framing**: how close the camera is.
    - **wide shot**: the whole room and everyone in it. Start a scene with one.
        - 💡 A face in a wide shot is only about 45 to 75 px wide and H3 draws in 16 px blocks, so faces and mouths can garble. Use a **medium shot**, **two-shot** or **over the shoulder** when a face or a line matters.
    - **side view**, **two-shot**: two people in frame.
    - **medium shot**: waist up. **close-up**: face and shoulders. **extreme close-up**: the face.
    - **over the shoulder**, **from behind**, **custom** (you describe it in the action).
- **who it's on**: the person the camera is on, **everyone**, or **nobody**.
    - **nobody**: an empty shot, the place alone (a ship coming out of hyperspace, an empty street). No faces are sent, and only a voiceover can speak.
- **move**: still, slow push-in, slow pull back, pan, tracking, orbit, handheld. Still is the safest.
- **✂ cut / 🎞 keep rolling**:
    - **cut**: a new shot. It gets the faces, the room and the anchor. Use it almost always.
    - **keep rolling**: no cut, the camera carries straight on from the end of the shot before. The faces and the room carry on from those frames, so it gets **no pictures**.
        - One exception: people who walk in (out of an empty shot, or someone new) get their face and outfit pictures, or H3 invents their faces.
    - 🔒 A keep rolling card **locks** the framing, the place, the 🌐 angle, the outfits, the 🖼 start frame and the 📐 boxes to the shot it rolls from (greyed out, "🔒 from shot N"). **Who is in it** stays yours: people can walk in.
        - Need a new framing or place? Change the shot it rolls from, or make this one a **cut**. H3 can't carry on into a new framing: it cuts by itself to a room it invents.
- **where**: the place. Empty = the same place as the shot before.
- **seconds**: empty (**auto**) fits the action and the line. Type a number to set it. A line that can't fit stretches the shot.
- **action**: what happens before the line. Short sentences, present tense, one thing each.
- **speaker** + **line**: who talks, and the words exactly as they say them. One line per shot.
- **after**: what happens after the line (optional).
    - 💡 The action plays before the line. Something that should happen once she has spoken (the cup arriving after she orders) goes here.
- **🌐** (optional): aim this shot's camera inside the place's 360 panorama yourself. Close-ups get an angle automatically; this overrides it. **behind** is what is behind the person in words ("the arched windows"). H3 follows words over pictures, so fill it in.
- **🖼 start** / **🏁 end**: the first or last frame of the shot (✨ in step 3, or yours). H3 copies a start frame exactly.
    - 🖼 start is for cuts. A keep rolling shot starts from the shot before (its slot is greyed out).
    - **🏁 end**: pin one only when the action ends on it ("she stops at the door"). A person who gets there early stands frozen.
- **📐**: draw boxes for who stands where (and props), on the shot's 🌐 angle. The storyboard uses them in step 3.
- **🎛 LoRA for this shot**: any LoRA for this shot only (a character, an outfit, a backdrop, a style, an action), on top of the LoRAs in the pipe. The next cut starts without it.
    - Pick it the same way as in the LC LoRA Loader: the folder picker, ◀ strength ▶, and **ℹ** for its trigger words. **✕** takes it off.
    - keep rolling uses the LoRAs of the shot it rolls from (🔒). A new LoRA mid-roll jumps at the join.
    - 💡 Character LoRAs: put the trigger word (usually the name) in the cast look and the action. One per person. A man and a woman with their own LoRAs held both faces; two women in one shot tend to blend, so give each her own close-up.
    - 💡 Name the outfit. A LoRA trained on less clothing brings less clothing unless a card says what they wear.
- **H3 prompt**: under each card, the shot's lines (see the top of this step). The Story's **warnings** (🛑 must fix, ⚠️ should look at) sit there too.
- **↑ ↓** move a shot up or down the list. **auto** (next to **seconds**, once you typed a number) puts the length back to automatic.
- **max_shot_seconds** (on the node, 20): the longest shot made in one go. Longer shots are made in parts that carry on from each other.

---

## ✍️ Prompting:
### 📖 **The full guide:** [H3 Showrunner Prompting Guide](https://github.com/lonecatone23/ComfyUI_LC_AV_nodes/blob/main/docs/showrunner/PROMPTING_GUIDE.md)

### The short version:

- **Looks**: one line each, head and hair only. Say the hair length, or H3 picks one.
- **Outfits**: a simple name on the card ("gym clothes"). The details go in its description, a color with a shade for every item: "faded olive jacket over a cream t-shirt".
- **Close-ups**: don't name the other person in the action. "Anika stares at Nova" made H3 cut to Nova halfway through Anika's close-up. "Anika stares across the table" kept her the whole shot. The Story warns you (⚠️).
- **Count props once**: "Each of them holds one cup." Or extras show up.
- **Name the prop like its card**: the card says "the red umbrella", the action says "Nova opens the red umbrella."
- **Close-ups across a table**: "Seen straight on from across the table, nobody in the foreground: the table edge runs along the bottom of the frame, her body square to the camera, eyes just past the lens to the left." Then say what is behind her.
- **No mouth actions during a line**: drinking or eating while talking loses the lips. The Story puts the cups down for you, but write the sip after the line.
- **Say what happens, not what doesn't**: "Nova sits still and listens", not "Nova doesn't move".

---

## Step 2: 📸 Make the pictures

- Press **✨** on a picture slot. The picture lands on its card by itself.
    - ✋ **Name the card first.** A blank name never writes over a picture.
    - If the slot already has a picture, ✨ asks first. The old one is kept: **↶** brings it back (the last 8 are kept).
- What each slot makes:
    - **cast card, headshot slot**: head and hair, calm neutral face, no clothes, on plain grey (1024 x 1024).
    - **cast card, 👗 slot**: the person head to toe in their outfit, from the **outfit notes** (896 x 1152).
    - **outfit card**: its **description** on the person who wears it, head to toe, on plain grey (896 x 1152). Nobody wears it: an invisible mannequin.
    - **place card, room slot**: the room, empty, the whole space in view (1344 x 768).
    - **place card, 🌐 slot**: the room all the way round (2:1) for the 360 view.
    - **prop card**: the object alone, on plain grey (1024 x 1024).
- ✋ **Cast, outfit and prop pictures always end up on plain grey**: drafted here or dropped in yourself, the background comes off (BiRefNet). A card's own background, props and expression leak into every shot it's in.
- 💡 Not happy? Press **✨** again: the seed changes every time. **↶** goes back to the one before.
- 💡 **Neutral faces only.** A smiling card gives you a smiling actor in every shot. It's not a hard lock, but it pulls.
- 💡 **360 panorama**: one per place. Make a few and keep one with a level horizon and nobody in it, then set **📷 the wide shot faces** on the place card once.
- 💡 **More control?** An art style or a size goes on **LC H3 Story Card Prompt** inside **Cards & Storyboard 🃏**. ✨ uses what is set there.
- 📚 **Or skip making them:** every cast, outfit, prop and 🌐 360 slot has a **📚 Library** tab in its picture picker: 102 ready-made pictures (30 cast headshots, 32 seasonal outfits, 24 props, 16 360 panoramas).
    - Click one: it downloads once and lands on the card. An empty card gets its name and text too.
    - Browse them all: [LC H3 Library on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lonecatone23/lc-h3-library)

---

## Step 3: 🗺️ Storyboard (optional, recommended)

The first frame of each shot, built from your cards, so every shot starts with the right people in the right room.

- On each shot card, press **📐** and draw a box for each person (and prop) where they should be. The boxes sit on the shot's 🌐 angle, so you place people on the view the shot will use. Pick who each box is.
- Press **✨** on the shot's **🖼 start** slot. **MOSS** lays the shot out from the boxes, then **Krea 2 Identity Edit** redraws it sharp with your cast cards. It lands in the slot.
    - **🏁 end** works the same for the frame a shot lands on.
    - One ✨ per frame.
- A later wide shot in a place you've already shown is built from the first wide shot's frame, so the room, the table and the camera side stay put.
    - ✋ **Box only who changes** (Nova coming back in the red dress). Everyone boxed is drawn again, and their face can drift.
- ✋ **The start frame is the action's first moment.** Nova already seated in the frame + "Nova comes back and sits down" gave a second Nova walking in. Box her where she comes from, or write the action from where the frame is.
- ✋ **H3 copies a start frame exactly.** A soft or wrong picture makes a soft or wrong shot. Press **✨** again for a new one, or **↶** for the one before.

---

## Step 4: 🎥 Make the movie

- Press **Run**. **Make** renders every shot that isn't made yet.
- One Run makes the whole movie, shot after shot, and joins it as it goes. 1 shot or 20.
- **Stop** ends it with nothing left in the queue. Run again and it picks up where it stopped.
- **The board** (under the shots on the Story node):
    - ✅ made, ✏️ changed since it was made, 🔒 locked.
    - ▶ plays a shot: its own part, without the second and a half it carries over from the shot before.
    - ↻ makes **that one shot** again with a new seed, then stops. Nothing after it is touched (the old take is kept in `takes/`).
        - 💡 A keep rolling shot right after it won't join smoothly until you ↻ it too.
    - 🔒 locks a keeper so nothing remakes it.
    - 🎬 plays the whole movie. **⟳** looks for new takes.
- **Long story?** ▾ next to a shot's number folds it to one line (▸ all / ▾ all in the 🎞 Shots header). The project bar (name, 📂, 💾) stays pinned at the top while you scroll.
- **Changed a shot?** It turns ✏️. Run remakes only the ✏️ shots, the rest stay.
- **info** (Make's text output) after every shot:
    - **face match**: 0.55 and up = same person, 0.40 to 0.55 = close, under 0.40 = someone else. Redo it.
    - **join**: how smooth each keep-rolling join is.

### 📌 Anchors: keeping the room the same
- **What it is:** a still frame of a place, saved on the place card's **📌 anchors** row. It shows H3 the room as it must stay: the furniture, the windows, who sits where.
- **Why:** on every cut H3 builds the room again. Without something to copy, the café gets a new counter, the table moves, and people swap seats.
- **Automatic** (Make's **hold_scene** on, the default): the first wide shot made in a place becomes its anchor. Every later cut there with **two or more people** gets it. A close-up of one person gets the room picture or its 360 view instead.
- **Your own** (better): play a made shot on the board (▶), pause on a frame where the room and everyone in it look right, press **📌 Room anchor**. The button turns green and says which anchor it added. It lands in that place's anchors row and replaces the automatic one. The **+** square in the row takes any picture.
- **🖼 Start shot N here** (same player): this frame becomes the **next** shot's 🖼 start frame, so the next shot opens exactly on it. A keep rolling next shot becomes a cut.
    - 💡 📌 only remembers the room. It never starts a shot. To start a shot on a frame, use 🖼.
- **Cutting back** to a setup you've already shown (same place, framing and person) opens on that shot's first frame by itself, so the camera, room and people match. Remake the first one and the cut-back is marked ✏️ too.
- Keep-rolling shots never get an anchor: they carry on from the frames before them.
- A storyboard start frame (step 3) beats an anchor: H3 copies it exactly. Anchors matter most for shots without one.
- × on an anchor removes it.

---

## Step 5: 🎞️ Post Processing (when the movie is done)

### ⚠️ It will not save unless **Save Video 💾** is switched on!
- Keep **Make** on: with every shot made it just hands over the finished movie. Nothing renders again.
- Turn on what you want in the panel, in this order:
    - **Load Video**: needed for everything below.
    - **Frame Interpolate** 24 → 48: about half the jitter for a sliver of detail. Under a minute.
    - **RTX Super Resolution**: **deblur** sharpens soft edges at the same size. Set **mode** to **upscale** for 2x instead. Needs an NVIDIA RTX card.
    - **Save Video 💾**: nothing saves without it.
    - **Audio Volume** and **Audio EQ**: louder or quieter, and a simple 3-band EQ for the voices. Leave them off if the sound is fine.

---

# ✋ Read this first

- **What this does:** you write a short movie on one node (who is in it, where it happens, and every shot), make a picture for each person and place, and press **Run**. It renders the shots one after another with MiniMax H3 and joins them into one movie with sound and dialogue.
- **Do the steps in order.** Every step uses what the step before it made. Skipping ahead is the fastest way to get strangers in random rooms.
- **💡 The guided tour:** open **Vision Assistant** (the left sidebar) → **Tour**. It lights up each part of the workflow in order and marks the settings that matter. Use it alongside this note.
- 🛑🚫 **Don't bypass nodes by hand.** **Cards & Storyboard 🃏** is bypassed on the inside on purpose. The **✨** buttons switch on what they need and put it back.
- ⚠️ This is a **long job** on a **big model**. 32 GB of VRAM is comfortable at 960 x 544. Less works, just slower.

## The basics
- **This workflow saves every step.** 
   - If you create images, video sections, etc., you can 💾 save the project, work on a different project, and come back to it or redo a section at any time.
   -  **Nothing is lost:** what finished stays finished.
- **Pictures and the movie are separate Runs:**
    - **Pictures:** press **✨** on a card's picture slot (steps 2 and 3). The Story switches on the part of **Cards & Storyboard 🃏** that makes it, keeps **Make 🎥** off, runs once and puts everything back.
    - **Movie:** press **Run** (step 4). **Make** renders every shot that isn't made yet.
    - ⚠️ **Make has to be off while a picture is made.** A new picture changes the shots that use it, and Make would render them again on the same Run. ✨ does that for you.
- **Save💾** Everything is saved in a **project** folder named on the Story node. Close ComfyUI, come back tomorrow, and it's all still there.

**🎨Post processing**
- Leave these switches off until you are ready to use it
- It processes the entire movie all at once and it is heavy, so I would not let it just run.
- Keep **Make 🎥** on (don't bypass it).

---

## ⚙️ Settings

- **megapixels**: 0.82 = 1216 x 672 (16:9). 0.52 (960 x 544) is faster, but faces in wide shots get very small.
   - Keep one size for the whole project. Change it anyway and the next Run makes every shot made at the old size again, in order (the 📐 size line lists them).
   - 💡 Don't stress too much over quality here. Push out decent, but 1 MP just slows down what you can upscale in the end.
- **Steps**: 12 with the turbo LoRA at 0.7 (the **Stock int8 + turbo LoRA 0.7** row in **Optimal setups and times ⏱️**). 8 with turbo at 1.0 is faster and a little softer. No turbo is slower and not better in my tests.
- **LC Seed**: the seed generator is the starting seed for H3 (each new shot) and the storyboard (MOSS and Krea 2: seed + shot number).
   - Every made shot keeps its own seed with its take, and ↻ (remake) always picks a new one.
   - The card pictures and post processing have their own seeds. Leave it alone.
- **Models & LoRAs**: the LC Optimizer picks the H3 files for your card. 
   - I suggest leaving it on **★ Recommended**.
   - I've tested it on other models. 10EROS works well, Singularity has voice issues. 
   - LoRAs. Your mileage will vary. 
- **Storyboard creator Models & Settings**: the models that make the pictures.
   - **Card Model (Krea2)** with the **Character or Style LoRA** makes the cast, outfit, place and prop pictures, and redraws the storyboard frames with the **🪪 Edit LoRA**.
   - **Storyboard model 📖 (MOSS)** lays the shots out from your boxes.
   - Leave both on **★ Recommended** unless you have your own.


---

## Step 1: 🎬 Write the story

Everything happens on the big **LC H3 Story** node. It has five lists: **🎭 Cast**, **👗 Outfits**, **📍 Places**, **👜 Props** and **🎞 Shots**.

- ✋ **The H3 prompt shows the shot's lines.** Make wraps the people, pictures and sound around them when the shot is made. Open a shot's **H3 prompt** to read it.
    - **↻** builds it again right now, so you see what will be sent before you spend time rendering.
    - **✎ Edit** lets you write it yourself. Your text is sent as written, and the cards stop changing it until you press **↶ Back to automatic**.
- **project name** (top): the folder everything is saved in, `output/LC_H3/<name>/`. Name it first. **📂** opens a saved project, **💾** saves now (every Run saves too). **💾 Save as** keeps a variant under a new name: the made shots come along and the original stays as it is.
- **📐 size** (under the project name): the size this project is made at (the last Run), with its aspect ratio. Shots made at another size are listed (⚠) and made again on the next Run.
- **The look of the whole movie** (top line): a few words for the film style ("cinematic, soft natural light, shallow depth of field"). It goes into every shot.

### 🖼 Picture slots
- Cast, outfit, place, 🌐 360, prop, 🖼 start and 🏁 end all work the same way.
    - Click a slot or drop a picture on it. **📚 Library** has ready-made ones, **⬆ Upload…** takes a file.
    - **✨** makes one for you (steps 2 and 3).
    - **↶** brings back the picture before this one. The last 8 are kept.
    - **✂** crops what the card uses of a picture (a head and shoulders out of a full-length photo, just the coat of an outfit).
    - **×** empties the slot (**↻** on a start or end frame).

### ✨ Write the story (optional)
- Type a short pitch ("Nova and Anika meet for coffee, Anika tells a story that goes too far, Nova leaves") and press **✨ Write the story**. A local model fills in the look, cast, places and shots once.
- After that it's plain text you edit. It never writes again unless you press the button again (which replaces the cards; pictures and voices on cards with the same name stay).
- Needs the **Story writer model** above. Pick it in the dropdown next to the button.
- **🔞 NSFW** (in the ✨ Write box, off by default): lets the writer write adult scenes, the same rule as LC Vision's NSFW style tag. Off, it writes the way it always has. Saved with the project.


### 🎭 Cast: one card per person
- **Name**: start with a capital letter. Shots find people by this exact name.
- **who**: woman, man, girl, boy, person, cat, dog. It tells people apart in the prompt.
- **look**: one line, the words H3 follows most. Describe the head and hair, then stop: age, face, eyes, freckles, skin, hair (length too). "mid twenties, a soft oval face, green eyes, light freckles, long wavy blonde hair". Never clothes: they go in the outfit picture.
    - ⚠️ No body words either (breasts, curvy, figure). Next to a bare-shouldered headshot they can make H3 leave the clothes off. The Story warns you (👗). The outfit picture shows the body.
- **face picture**: a headshot, made in step 2 (✨ on the slot), or yours (click the square or drop a picture on it). The background is automatically removed and the face is placed on a plain grey background to prevent it from bleeding into the scene or outfit.
    - Headshot means head and hair. No shoulders, no clothes: clothes in a headshot beat every outfit picture.
- **👗 outfit picture**: what they wear from their first shot, head to toe. Made in step 2 (✨ on the 👗 slot), or yours.
    - **outfit notes**: the whole outfit in detail. The picture is made from it, and H3 reads only its first piece of clothing as the outfit's name ("dark blue jumpsuit"). Start with the main piece and its color.
- **🎤 voice** (optional): a 2 to 15 s clip of how they sound. H3 copies the voice, not the words.
- **📋** copies the name and look to paste into another workflow.

### 👗 Outfits: the clothes, one card per outfit
- ✋ **Everyone needs clothes from somewhere.** The headshot carries none. Give each person a 👗 outfit picture on their cast card. With none, they get different clothes in every shot, and the Story warns you (👗).
- An outfit card is a change of clothes.
    - It can also be a state of dress: "naked", "topless, black jeans", "wrapped in a white towel". H3 gets it as written.
- **name**: a simple name: "red cocktail dress", "yoga outfit", "gym clothes". With a picture, it's all H3 reads about the outfit.
    - Never a list of pieces. Shoes and pants in the words pull close-ups wide (the Story warns you).
- **who wears it**: the person.
- **description**: the whole outfit head to toe, in detail, **a color for every item**, with the shade: "an off the shoulder grey cutoff sweatshirt, high waisted black leggings with a cross stitch band, white Nike gym shoes". Only the picture is made from it.
    - Layers outside first, with "over". Patterns name their colors ("floral blouse in pale peach and green"). Fabric helps (denim, silk, knit, leather).
- **picture**: made in step 2 (✨ on the slot: the person who wears it, head to toe, on plain grey), or yours. It carries every detail the name doesn't say.
- **How it plays:**
    - Everyone starts in their cast card's 👗 outfit. To change, pick another on a shot with **👗**, or name it in the action ("Nova comes back in the red dress"). They stay in it from that shot on.
    - Each shot gets "wearing <name>" in the prompt and the outfit picture. Close-ups stay close: no pants or shoes in the words.
    - Tested: a one-strap red dress with silver details came through from the picture alone, named just "red dress".
    - ⚠️ **Mismatched reference**: a cut back to an earlier camera opens on that shot's first frame, and a wide takes its room from the place's first wide. If that frame shows other clothes, people or props, the Story warns you. Pin a start frame, or give the scene its own place card.

### 📍 Places: one card per location
- **name**: "the cafe". Shots pick their place by this name.
- **sound**: sounds you can hear, nothing else: "rain on the glass, cups clinking, footsteps".
    - ✋ **Never write who speaks** ("nobody speaks", "no voices"). Naming speech makes H3 speak: the same silent shot talked in French and English with it and was silent without it. The Story adds "Nobody speaks." to a shot with no line by itself.
- **description**: what is there: the room, the furniture, the light.
- **room picture**: the place, **empty**. Made in step 2 (✨ on the slot), or yours.
- **🌐 360** (recommended): **one** panorama of the whole room (step 2, ✨ on the 🌐 slot). You don't make a picture per shot: the Story cuts each shot's view out of it by itself.
    - **Set it once:** turn the small viewer under the place until it shows what your wide shot shows (**📷 the wide shot faces**). That is "front". Every angle counts from there: 90 = right side of the room, -90 = left, 180 = behind the camera.
    - **Close-ups and medium shots get their view automatically.** One across the table from someone who already has an angle gets the reverse angle (+180), so the two of them have opposite sides of the room behind them. The others face the way the wide shot faces.
    - **Want a different angle?** Press **🌐** on the shot card and drag the view. Your angle always wins over the automatic one.
    - The view is cut as a flat picture (in the project's `views/` folder) and used as that shot's background, by Make and by the storyboard.
    - Wide shots use the room picture and the anchor, unless you aim them with 🌐 too.
- **📌 anchors**: frames that keep this room the same across cuts. Empty at first: see **📌 Anchors** below.

### 👜 Props: one card per object that matters
- Only for an object that must look the same in every shot (the red umbrella, the letter, the ring).
- **name**: "the red umbrella". ✋ Use these **exact words** in a shot's action, and that shot gets the prop's picture.
- **description**: what it looks like.
- **picture**: made in step 2 (✨ on the slot), or yours. It goes on plain grey like the cast.


**💡 Need something simple?** 
- Every cast, outfit, prop and 🌐 360 slot has a 📚 Library tab in its picture picker: 102 ready-made pictures (30 cast headshots, 32 seasonal outfits, 24 props, 16 360 panoramas). Browse them all: [LC H3 Library on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lonecatone23/lc-h3-library)


### 🎞 Shots: one card per shot, top to bottom is the movie
- **framing**: how close the camera is.
    - **wide shot**: the whole room and everyone in it. Start a scene with one.
        - 💡 A face in a wide shot is only about 45 to 75 px wide and H3 draws in 16 px blocks, so faces and mouths can garble. Use a **medium shot**, **two-shot** or **over the shoulder** when a face or a line matters.
    - **side view**, **two-shot**: two people in frame.
    - **medium shot**: waist up. **close-up**: face and shoulders. **extreme close-up**: the face.
    - **over the shoulder**, **from behind**, **custom** (you describe it in the action).
- **who it's on**: the person the camera is on, **everyone**, or **nobody**.
    - **nobody**: an empty shot, the place alone (a ship coming out of hyperspace, an empty street). No faces are sent, and only a voiceover can speak.
- **move**: still, slow push-in, slow pull back, pan, tracking, orbit, handheld. Still is the safest.
- **✂ cut / 🎞 keep rolling**:
    - **cut**: a new shot. It gets the faces, the room and the anchor. Use it almost always.
    - **keep rolling**: no cut, the camera carries straight on from the end of the shot before. The faces and the room carry on from those frames, so it gets **no pictures**.
        - One exception: people who walk in (out of an empty shot, or someone new) get their face and outfit pictures, or H3 invents their faces.
    - 🔒 A keep rolling card **locks** the framing, the place, the 🌐 angle, the outfits, the 🖼 start frame and the 📐 boxes to the shot it rolls from (greyed out, "🔒 from shot N"). **Who is in it** stays yours: people can walk in.
        - Need a new framing or place? Change the shot it rolls from, or make this one a **cut**. H3 can't carry on into a new framing: it cuts by itself to a room it invents.
- **where**: the place. Empty = the same place as the shot before.
- **seconds**: empty (**auto**) fits the action and the line. Type a number to set it. A line that can't fit stretches the shot.
- **action**: what happens before the line. Short sentences, present tense, one thing each.
- **speaker** + **line**: who talks, and the words exactly as they say them. One line per shot.
- **after**: what happens after the line (optional).
    - 💡 The action plays before the line. Something that should happen once she has spoken (the cup arriving after she orders) goes here.
- **🌐** (optional): aim this shot's camera inside the place's 360 panorama yourself. Close-ups get an angle automatically; this overrides it. **behind** is what is behind the person in words ("the arched windows"). H3 follows words over pictures, so fill it in.
- **🖼 start** / **🏁 end**: the first or last frame of the shot (✨ in step 3, or yours). H3 copies a start frame exactly.
    - 🖼 start is for cuts. A keep rolling shot starts from the shot before (its slot is greyed out).
    - **🏁 end**: pin one only when the action ends on it ("she stops at the door"). A person who gets there early stands frozen.
- **📐**: draw boxes for who stands where (and props), on the shot's 🌐 angle. The storyboard uses them in step 3.
- **🎛 LoRA for this shot**: any LoRA for this shot only (a character, an outfit, a backdrop, a style, an action), on top of the LoRAs in the pipe. The next cut starts without it.
    - Pick it the same way as in the LC LoRA Loader: the folder picker, ◀ strength ▶, and **ℹ** for its trigger words. **✕** takes it off.
    - keep rolling uses the LoRAs of the shot it rolls from (🔒). A new LoRA mid-roll jumps at the join.
    - 💡 Character LoRAs: put the trigger word (usually the name) in the cast look and the action. One per person. A man and a woman with their own LoRAs held both faces; two women in one shot tend to blend, so give each her own close-up.
    - 💡 Name the outfit. A LoRA trained on less clothing brings less clothing unless a card says what they wear.
- **H3 prompt**: under each card, the shot's lines (see the top of this step). The Story's **warnings** (🛑 must fix, ⚠️ should look at) sit there too.
- **↑ ↓** move a shot up or down the list. **auto** (next to **seconds**, once you typed a number) puts the length back to automatic.
- **max_shot_seconds** (on the node, 20): the longest shot made in one go. Longer shots are made in parts that carry on from each other.

---

## ✍️ Prompting:
### 📖 **The full guide:** [H3 Showrunner Prompting Guide](https://github.com/lonecatone23/ComfyUI_LC_AV_nodes/blob/main/docs/showrunner/PROMPTING_GUIDE.md)

### The short version:

- **Looks**: one line each, head and hair only. Say the hair length, or H3 picks one.
- **Outfits**: a simple name on the card ("gym clothes"). The details go in its description, a color with a shade for every item: "faded olive jacket over a cream t-shirt".
- **Close-ups**: don't name the other person in the action. "Anika stares at Nova" made H3 cut to Nova halfway through Anika's close-up. "Anika stares across the table" kept her the whole shot. The Story warns you (⚠️).
- **Count props once**: "Each of them holds one cup." Or extras show up.
- **Name the prop like its card**: the card says "the red umbrella", the action says "Nova opens the red umbrella."
- **Close-ups across a table**: "Seen straight on from across the table, nobody in the foreground: the table edge runs along the bottom of the frame, her body square to the camera, eyes just past the lens to the left." Then say what is behind her.
- **No mouth actions during a line**: drinking or eating while talking loses the lips. The Story puts the cups down for you, but write the sip after the line.
- **Say what happens, not what doesn't**: "Nova sits still and listens", not "Nova doesn't move".

---

## Step 2: 📸 Make the pictures

- Press **✨** on a picture slot. The picture lands on its card by itself.
    - ✋ **Name the card first.** A blank name never writes over a picture.
    - If the slot already has a picture, ✨ asks first. The old one is kept: **↶** brings it back (the last 8 are kept).
- What each slot makes:
    - **cast card, headshot slot**: head and hair, calm neutral face, no clothes, on plain grey (1024 x 1024).
    - **cast card, 👗 slot**: the person head to toe in their outfit, from the **outfit notes** (896 x 1152).
    - **outfit card**: its **description** on the person who wears it, head to toe, on plain grey (896 x 1152). Nobody wears it: an invisible mannequin.
    - **place card, room slot**: the room, empty, the whole space in view (1344 x 768).
    - **place card, 🌐 slot**: the room all the way round (2:1) for the 360 view.
    - **prop card**: the object alone, on plain grey (1024 x 1024).
- ✋ **Cast, outfit and prop pictures always end up on plain grey**: drafted here or dropped in yourself, the background comes off (BiRefNet). A card's own background, props and expression leak into every shot it's in.
- 💡 Not happy? Press **✨** again: the seed changes every time. **↶** goes back to the one before.
- 💡 **Neutral faces only.** A smiling card gives you a smiling actor in every shot. It's not a hard lock, but it pulls.
- 💡 **360 panorama**: one per place. Make a few and keep one with a level horizon and nobody in it, then set **📷 the wide shot faces** on the place card once.
- 💡 **More control?** An art style or a size goes on **LC H3 Story Card Prompt** inside **Cards & Storyboard 🃏**. ✨ uses what is set there.
- 📚 **Or skip making them:** every cast, outfit, prop and 🌐 360 slot has a **📚 Library** tab in its picture picker: 102 ready-made pictures (30 cast headshots, 32 seasonal outfits, 24 props, 16 360 panoramas).
    - Click one: it downloads once and lands on the card. An empty card gets its name and text too.
    - Browse them all: [LC H3 Library on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lonecatone23/lc-h3-library)

---

## Step 3: 🗺️ Storyboard (optional, recommended)

The first frame of each shot, built from your cards, so every shot starts with the right people in the right room.

- On each shot card, press **📐** and draw a box for each person (and prop) where they should be. The boxes sit on the shot's 🌐 angle, so you place people on the view the shot will use. Pick who each box is.
- Press **✨** on the shot's **🖼 start** slot. **MOSS** lays the shot out from the boxes, then **Krea 2 Identity Edit** redraws it sharp with your cast cards. It lands in the slot.
    - **🏁 end** works the same for the frame a shot lands on.
    - One ✨ per frame.
- A later wide shot in a place you've already shown is built from the first wide shot's frame, so the room, the table and the camera side stay put.
    - ✋ **Box only who changes** (Nova coming back in the red dress). Everyone boxed is drawn again, and their face can drift.
- ✋ **The start frame is the action's first moment.** Nova already seated in the frame + "Nova comes back and sits down" gave a second Nova walking in. Box her where she comes from, or write the action from where the frame is.
- ✋ **H3 copies a start frame exactly.** A soft or wrong picture makes a soft or wrong shot. Press **✨** again for a new one, or **↶** for the one before.

---

## Step 4: 🎥 Make the movie

- Press **Run**. **Make** renders every shot that isn't made yet.
- One Run makes the whole movie, shot after shot, and joins it as it goes. 1 shot or 20.
- **Stop** ends it with nothing left in the queue. Run again and it picks up where it stopped.
- **The board** (under the shots on the Story node):
    - ✅ made, ✏️ changed since it was made, 🔒 locked.
    - ▶ plays a shot: its own part, without the second and a half it carries over from the shot before.
    - ↻ makes **that one shot** again with a new seed, then stops. Nothing after it is touched (the old take is kept in `takes/`).
        - 💡 A keep rolling shot right after it won't join smoothly until you ↻ it too.
    - 🔒 locks a keeper so nothing remakes it.
    - 🎬 plays the whole movie. **⟳** looks for new takes.
- **Long story?** ▾ next to a shot's number folds it to one line (▸ all / ▾ all in the 🎞 Shots header). The project bar (name, 📂, 💾) stays pinned at the top while you scroll.
- **Changed a shot?** It turns ✏️. Run remakes only the ✏️ shots, the rest stay.
- **info** (Make's text output) after every shot:
    - **face match**: 0.55 and up = same person, 0.40 to 0.55 = close, under 0.40 = someone else. Redo it.
    - **join**: how smooth each keep-rolling join is.

### 📌 Anchors: keeping the room the same
- **What it is:** a still frame of a place, saved on the place card's **📌 anchors** row. It shows H3 the room as it must stay: the furniture, the windows, who sits where.
- **Why:** on every cut H3 builds the room again. Without something to copy, the café gets a new counter, the table moves, and people swap seats.
- **Automatic** (Make's **hold_scene** on, the default): the first wide shot made in a place becomes its anchor. Every later cut there with **two or more people** gets it. A close-up of one person gets the room picture or its 360 view instead.
- **Your own** (better): play a made shot on the board (▶), pause on a frame where the room and everyone in it look right, press **📌 Room anchor**. The button turns green and says which anchor it added. It lands in that place's anchors row and replaces the automatic one. The **+** square in the row takes any picture.
- **🖼 Start shot N here** (same player): this frame becomes the **next** shot's 🖼 start frame, so the next shot opens exactly on it. A keep rolling next shot becomes a cut.
    - 💡 📌 only remembers the room. It never starts a shot. To start a shot on a frame, use 🖼.
- **Cutting back** to a setup you've already shown (same place, framing and person) opens on that shot's first frame by itself, so the camera, room and people match. Remake the first one and the cut-back is marked ✏️ too.
- Keep-rolling shots never get an anchor: they carry on from the frames before them.
- A storyboard start frame (step 3) beats an anchor: H3 copies it exactly. Anchors matter most for shots without one.
- × on an anchor removes it.

---

## Step 5: 🎞️ Post Processing (when the movie is done)

### ⚠️ It will not save unless **Save Video 💾** is switched on!
- Keep **Make** on: with every shot made it just hands over the finished movie. Nothing renders again.
- Turn on what you want in the panel, in this order:
    - **Load Video**: needed for everything below.
    - **Frame Interpolate** 24 → 48: about half the jitter for a sliver of detail. Under a minute.
    - **RTX Super Resolution**: **deblur** sharpens soft edges at the same size. Set **mode** to **upscale** for 2x instead. Needs an NVIDIA RTX card.
    - **Save Video 💾**: nothing saves without it.
    - **Audio Volume** and **Audio EQ**: louder or quieter, and a simple 3-band EQ for the voices. Leave them off if the sound is fine.

---

### File Storage Locations

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   │   ├── Krealism V3.1
│   │   └── moss_image_sft_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 text_encoders/
│   │   ├── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
│   │   ├── qwen3vl_4b Heretic (or qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled)
│   │   └── qwen3.5_9b_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
│   │   ├── krea2RealVae_v10.safetensors
│   │   └── flux2-vae_small.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 vae_approx/
│   │   └── taeh3.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 loras/
│   │   ├── 📂 MiniMax/
│   │   │   ├── minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_comfyui_bf16.safetensors
│   │   │   ├── MMH3-RealismSlider-V1.safetensors
│   │   │   └── mvmt_h3_lora_v1_500.safetensors
│   │   └── 📂 Krea 2/
│   │       └── krea2_identity_edit_v2.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 LLM/
│   │   └── Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-abliterated-v2 GGUF (+ its mmproj)
│   ├── 📂 background_removal/
│   │   └── BiRefNet-general.safetensors (downloads on first use)
│   ├── 📂 facerestore/
│   │   └── yunet + sface .onnx (optional)
│   └── 📂 rife/ (downloads on first use)
├── 📂 input/
│   └── 📂 lc_h3_refs/
│       └── 📂 <project>/
│           ├── cast_, place_, pano_, prop_ pictures
│           └── start_ and end_ frames
└── 📂 output/
    └── 📂 LC_H3/
        └── 📂 <project>/
            ├── story.json, plan.json
            ├── <project>.mp4 (the finished movie)
            ├── 📂 views/ (the 360 angles)
            └── 📂 takes/
                ├── seg_001.mp4, seg_002.mp4, etc.
                └── old takes (nothing is ever deleted)
```

---

*"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"*- Yoda Auditore, **Assassin's Wars**

nodes.title: LC123 Settings ⚙️

en.text:
# LC123 Settings ⚙️

**Where are they?** Open **Settings** (the gear), then **LC123 Settings ⚙️**. There are five sections: **Align**, **Connections**, **Notes**, **Optimization** and **Performance**.

- 💡 Missing a setting? Restart ComfyUI, then press **Ctrl+F5** so the browser loads the new files.

---

### 📐 Align

**Align tool**
- Default: **On**
- The switch for the whole tool. Off = no **Align** button (the LC logo) in the top toolbar and none of the features below.
- With it on, the **Align** button turns Align on or off **for the open workflow**: light gray with the red flame = on, dark gray with a gray flame = off.
    - That on/off is saved in the workflow. Save it with Align on and it opens with Align on, even on a fresh ComfyUI.
    - Every workflow tab keeps its own. Switch tabs and the tool follows that tab (on in one, off in the other, no mix-ups).
    - Turning it on or off counts as a change to the workflow, so you get the unsaved dot.
- Nodes snap to **Node lines**, groups snap to **Group lines**. A line lights up when you get close.
- Works on the classic canvas and in **Nodes 2.0**.
- **Snap distance** is ComfyUI's own **Snap to grid size** (Settings > Lite Graph > Canvas). Smaller grid = tighter snap. New lines land on that grid too.
    - **Shift** while dragging hands the drag to ComfyUI's own grid snap (no line snap). With **Always snap to grid** on, a line snap still wins on the axis it caught.

**Rulers**
- Default: **On**
- Rulers on the top and left edge while Align is on:
    - **Left click** a ruler: adds a **Node line** (blue). Nodes snap to it.
    - **Right click** a ruler: adds a **Group line** (orange). Groups snap to it.
    - Click a line's marker again to remove it. Drag a marker to move it.
- Lines save with the workflow.

**Line reveal distance (px)**
- Default: **120**
- Lines stay invisible until the cursor or whatever you drag gets this close.

**Also snap to other nodes and groups**
- Default: **Off**
- On = also snap to other nodes' edges and centers (no line is shown for those).

---

### 🔌 Connections

**Connection FX**
- Default: **Off**
- While you drag a wire, every socket it can plug into glows in its socket color.
- Get close and rings pulse out of the socket. Closer = bigger and brighter.
- **Connection FX reach (px):** how close the cursor has to be before the rings start. Default 160.
- **Connection FX zoomed-out glow (%):** zoomed out, every valid socket glows brighter so you can find it. Default 60.
- Classic canvas only. With **Nodes 2.0** on it stays out of the way.

---



---

### 🩺 Optimization

**Optimization report**
- One button. It pans the canvas by itself for a few seconds, times what every pack in the open workflow draws and runs, and scans their files.
- You get a list of what slows your canvas down, biggest first, sorted into:
    - **That pack's own settings** (the exact setting name, where it lives and its current value)
    - **LC123 optimization settings**
    - **ComfyUI settings**
    - **Sidebar tabs**
    - **Required to function** (no setting, it is how that pack works)
- Only node packs used in the open workflow are analyzed.
- Every setting it suggests is checked against its current value:
    - ⚠️ big gain · ✅ worthwhile gain · 💡 small gain
    - ⚪ already set · ➖ does not apply · ℹ️ required, no setting for it
- **Show last run:** the button at the top flips to the previous report. Each new run also shows what got faster and which fixes are done since last time.
    - Only the last run is kept (it survives a refresh). Each run replaces it.
- Nothing is changed. (Keep the mouse still while it runs.)
- 💡 Also in the right-click menu on the empty canvas.

---

### ⚡ Performance

These only change what you see on the canvas. Generation, VRAM, **Save Image** and every **IMAGE** output stay full resolution. (A lighter preview never means a lighter image.)

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove wipe** | Off | Turns off the hover A/B wipe on LC image FX nodes. The last result still shows. |
| **Half-resolution previews** | Off | Draws FX previews at half size. Less work while panning. |
| **Clamp longest side** | Off | Shrinks on-node previews so the longest side fits **Max edge**. |
| **Max edge (px)** | 768 | Only used when **Clamp longest side** is on. Range 256 to 2048. Try 512 on heavy graphs. |
| **No preview when collapsed** | On | Collapsed FX nodes skip drawing their preview. |
| **Hide FX on-node previews** | Off | Hides every LC image FX preview. |
| **Recent colors** | On | Keeps your last 8 custom colors in the right-click **Colors** menu. Adds a Custom picker if Custom Scripts is not installed. |
| **Skin Beauty full preview override** | On | **LC Skin Beauty** keeps a full-quality preview even with half-res or clamp on, so you can still zoom into skin. Wipe still follows **Remove wipe**. |
| **LoRA loader info button** | On | Shows the ℹ button on each **LC LoRA Loader** row. Trigger words come from the LoRA file itself (no internet). Turn off to declutter. |
| **Preview distance (px)** | 40 | Like node text, an on-node image switches off when you zoom out far enough that it is drawn smaller than this. Smaller previews switch off first. 0 = always draw. |

**Never affected:** **LC Image Compare 🔎**, **LC Image Split 🖼️** and **LC Dynamic Overlay** keep their full preview and wipe no matter what (only **Preview distance** switches them off when zoomed far out).

**Suggested setups**
- **Normal use:** leave everything at default.
- **Laggy graph:** turn on **Half-resolution previews** and **Clamp longest side** (Max edge 512). Keep **No preview when collapsed** on.
- **Lightest canvas:** turn on **Hide FX on-node previews**. Use **Image Compare** or **Image Split** when you need to see a before/after.
- 💡 Changes apply on the next redraw. Pan the canvas a little, no restart needed.

---

"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"- Yoda Auditore, Assassin's Wars

zh.text:
# LC123 Settings ⚙️

**在哪里？** 打开 **Settings**（齿轮），然后找 **LC123 Settings ⚙️**。共有五个部分：**Align**、**Connections**、**Notes**、**Optimization** 和 **Performance**。

- 💡 找不到某个设置？重启 ComfyUI，然后按 **Ctrl+F5**，让浏览器加载新文件。

---

### 📐 Align

**Align tool**
- 默认：**开**
- 整个工具的总开关。关 = 顶部工具栏里没有 **Align** 按钮（LC 标志），下面所有功能也都没有。
- 打开后，**Align** 按钮用来**为当前打开的工作流**开关 Align：浅灰色带红色火焰 = 开，深灰色带灰色火焰 = 关。
    - 这个开关状态会保存在工作流里。开着 Align 保存，之后即使在全新的 ComfyUI 里打开也是开着的。
    - 每个工作流标签页各自独立。切换标签页，工具会跟着该标签页走（一个开一个关，不会混）。
    - 开关会算作对工作流的修改，所以会出现未保存的小圆点。
- 节点吸附到 **Node lines**，分组吸附到 **Group lines**。靠近时线会亮起来。
- 在经典画布和 **Nodes 2.0** 中都能用。
- **Snap distance** 就是 ComfyUI 自带的 **Snap to grid size**（Settings > Lite Graph > Canvas）。网格越小，吸附越紧。新线也会落在这个网格上。
    - 拖动时按 **Shift** 会把拖动交给 ComfyUI 自带的网格吸附（不吸附到线）。开启 **Always snap to grid** 时，在已被线吸住的那个轴上，线吸附仍然优先。

**Rulers**
- 默认：**开**
- Align 开启时，顶部和左侧边缘会显示标尺：
    - 在标尺上**左键点击**：添加一条 **Node line**（蓝色）。节点会吸附到它。
    - 在标尺上**右键点击**：添加一条 **Group line**（橙色）。分组会吸附到它。
    - 再次点击线的标记可删除。拖动标记可移动。
- 线会随工作流保存。

**Line reveal distance (px)**
- 默认：**120**
- 线一直不可见，直到光标或你拖动的东西靠近到这个距离。

**Also snap to other nodes and groups**
- 默认：**关**
- 开 = 还会吸附到其他节点的边缘和中心（这些不会显示线）。

---

### 🔌 Connections

**Connection FX**
- 默认：**关**
- 拖动连线时，每个它能接入的接口都会以接口自己的颜色发光。
- 靠近时，接口会向外脉冲出圆环。越近 = 越大越亮。
- **Connection FX reach (px)：** 光标要靠多近圆环才开始出现。默认 160。
- **Connection FX zoomed-out glow (%)：** 缩小视图时，每个有效接口会更亮，方便你找到。默认 60。
- 仅限经典画布。开启 **Nodes 2.0** 时它会自动避开。

---



---

### 🩺 Optimization

**Optimization report**
- 一个按钮。它会自己平移画布几秒钟，测量当前工作流里每个包的绘制和运行耗时，并扫描它们的文件。
- 你会得到一份拖慢画布的清单，最慢的排最前，分为：
    - **该包自己的设置**（确切的设置名、所在位置和当前值）
    - **LC123 优化设置**
    - **ComfyUI 设置**
    - **侧边栏标签页**
    - **功能必需**（没有设置项，这个包本来就是这样工作的）
- 只分析当前工作流里用到的节点包。
- 它建议的每个设置都会对照当前值检查：
    - ⚠️ 收益很大 · ✅ 值得的收益 · 💡 收益较小
    - ⚪ 已设置 · ➖ 不适用 · ℹ️ 必需，没有对应设置
- **Show last run：** 顶部的按钮可切换到上一份报告。每次新运行还会显示相比上次哪些变快了、哪些修复已经完成。
    - 只保留最近一次（刷新后仍在）。每次运行会替换它。
- 不会更改任何东西。（运行期间请保持鼠标不动。）
- 💡 在空白画布上右键菜单里也有。

---

### ⚡ Performance

这些只改变你在画布上看到的内容。生成、VRAM、**Save Image** 以及每个 **IMAGE** 输出都保持完整分辨率。（预览变轻不代表图像变轻。）

| 设置 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove wipe** | 关 | 关闭 LC 图像 FX 节点上悬停的 A/B 擦除对比。最后一次的结果仍会显示。 |
| **Half-resolution previews** | 关 | 以一半大小绘制 FX 预览。平移时负担更轻。 |
| **Clamp longest side** | 关 | 缩小节点上的预览，让最长边适配 **Max edge**。 |
| **Max edge (px)** | 768 | 仅在 **Clamp longest side** 开启时使用。范围 256 到 2048。重型图表可试 512。 |
| **No preview when collapsed** | 开 | 折叠的 FX 节点不绘制预览。 |
| **Hide FX on-node previews** | 关 | 隐藏所有 LC 图像 FX 预览。 |
| **Recent colors** | 开 | 在右键 **Colors** 菜单里保留你最近的 8 个自定义颜色。如果没装 Custom Scripts，会补上一个 Custom 取色器。 |
| **Skin Beauty full preview override** | 开 | 即使开了半分辨率或限制尺寸，**LC Skin Beauty** 仍保留完整质量预览，方便你放大看皮肤。Wipe 仍遵循 **Remove wipe**。 |
| **LoRA loader info button** | 开 | 在每个 **LC LoRA Loader** 行上显示 ℹ 按钮。触发词来自 LoRA 文件本身（无需联网）。关闭可让界面更简洁。 |
| **Preview distance (px)** | 40 | 和节点文字一样，当你缩小到节点上的图像绘制尺寸小于这个值时，它就会关闭。较小的预览先关闭。0 = 始终绘制。 |

**从不受影响：** **LC Image Compare 🔎**、**LC Image Split 🖼️** 和 **LC Dynamic Overlay** 无论如何都保留完整预览和擦除对比（只有 **Preview distance** 会在缩得很小时把它们关闭）。

**推荐方案**
- **正常使用：** 全部保持默认。
- **图表卡顿：** 开启 **Half-resolution previews** 和 **Clamp longest side**（Max edge 512）。保持 **No preview when collapsed** 开启。
- **最轻量的画布：** 开启 **Hide FX on-node previews**。需要看前后对比时用 **Image Compare** 或 **Image Split**。
- 💡 修改会在下次重绘时生效。稍微平移一下画布即可，无需重启。

---

"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"- Yoda Auditore, Assassin's Wars

ja.text:
# LC123 Settings ⚙️

**どこにある?** **Settings**(歯車)を開き、**LC123 Settings ⚙️** を選びます。**Align**、**Connections**、**Notes**、**Optimization**、**Performance** の5つのセクションがあります。

- 💡 設定が見当たらない? ComfyUI を再起動してから **Ctrl+F5** を押し、ブラウザに新しいファイルを読み込ませてください。

---

### 📐 Align

**Align tool**
- デフォルト: **On**
- ツール全体のスイッチです。Off = 上部ツールバーの **Align** ボタン(LC ロゴ)も、以下の機能もすべてなくなります。
- オンにすると、**Align** ボタンで**開いているワークフロー**の Align をオン/オフできます。ライトグレーに赤い炎 = オン、ダークグレーにグレーの炎 = オフです。
    - そのオン/オフはワークフローに保存されます。Align をオンにして保存すれば、新しい ComfyUI でもオンで開きます。
    - ワークフローのタブごとに独立して保持されます。タブを切り替えると、ツールもそのタブに従います(片方でオン、もう片方でオフ、混ざることはありません)。
    - オン/オフの切り替えはワークフローの変更として扱われるので、未保存のドットが付きます。
- ノードは **Node lines** に、グループは **Group lines** にスナップします。近づくとラインが光ります。
- クラシックキャンバスでも **Nodes 2.0** でも動作します。
- **Snap distance** は ComfyUI 自体の **Snap to grid size**(Settings > Lite Graph > Canvas)です。グリッドが小さいほどスナップが細かくなります。新しいラインもそのグリッドに乗ります。
    - ドラッグ中に **Shift** を押すと、ドラッグが ComfyUI 自体のグリッドスナップに切り替わります(ラインスナップなし)。**Always snap to grid** がオンの場合でも、ラインに捕まった軸ではラインスナップが優先されます。

**Rulers**
- デフォルト: **On**
- Align がオンのとき、上端と左端にルーラーが表示されます:
    - ルーラーを**左クリック**: **Node line**(青)を追加します。ノードがスナップします。
    - ルーラーを**右クリック**: **Group line**(オレンジ)を追加します。グループがスナップします。
    - ラインのマーカーをもう一度クリックすると削除されます。マーカーをドラッグすると移動できます。
- ラインはワークフローと一緒に保存されます。

**Line reveal distance (px)**
- デフォルト: **120**
- カーソル、またはドラッグ中のものがこの距離まで近づくまで、ラインは見えません。

**Also snap to other nodes and groups**
- デフォルト: **Off**
- On = 他のノードの端や中心にもスナップします(それらのラインは表示されません)。

---

### 🔌 Connections

**Connection FX**
- デフォルト: **Off**
- ワイヤーをドラッグしている間、接続可能なすべてのソケットが、そのソケットの色で光ります。
- 近づくと、ソケットからリングが波打ちます。近いほど大きく、明るくなります。
- **Connection FX reach (px):** リングが出始めるまでにカーソルがどれだけ近づく必要があるかです。デフォルトは 160。
- **Connection FX zoomed-out glow (%):** ズームアウトしたとき、有効なソケットがより明るく光るので見つけやすくなります。デフォルトは 60。
- クラシックキャンバス専用です。**Nodes 2.0** がオンのときは邪魔をしません。

---



---

### 🩺 Optimization

**Optimization report**
- ボタンが1つあります。キャンバスを数秒間自動でパンし、開いているワークフロー内の各パックの描画と実行にかかる時間を計測し、そのファイルをスキャンします。
- キャンバスを重くしているものが、影響の大きい順にリストされ、次のように分類されます:
    - **そのパック自身の設定**(正確な設定名、その場所、現在の値)
    - **LC123 optimization settings**
    - **ComfyUI settings**
    - **Sidebar tabs**
    - **Required to function**(設定なし、そのパックの仕組み上必要なもの)
- 開いているワークフローで使われているノードパックだけが分析されます。
- 提案されるすべての設定は、現在の値と照合されます:
    - ⚠️ 大きな効果 · ✅ 価値のある効果 · 💡 小さな効果
    - ⚪ 設定済み · ➖ 該当なし · ℹ️ 必須、設定なし
- **Show last run:** 上部のボタンで前回のレポートに切り替わります。新しい実行のたびに、前回から速くなった点と、完了した修正も表示されます。
    - 保持されるのは最後の実行だけです(更新しても残ります)。実行のたびに置き換わります。
- 何も変更されません。(実行中はマウスを動かさないでください。)
- 💡 空のキャンバスを右クリックしたメニューにもあります。

---

### ⚡ Performance

これらはキャンバス上の見た目だけを変えます。生成、VRAM、**Save Image**、すべての **IMAGE** 出力はフル解像度のままです。(プレビューが軽くなっても、画像が軽くなることはありません。)

| Setting | Default | 機能 |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove wipe** | Off | LC image FX ノードのホバー A/B ワイプをオフにします。最後の結果は表示されたままです。 |
| **Half-resolution previews** | Off | FX プレビューを半分のサイズで描画します。パン中の負荷が減ります。 |
| **Clamp longest side** | Off | ノード上のプレビューを、長辺が **Max edge** に収まるよう縮小します。 |
| **Max edge (px)** | 768 | **Clamp longest side** がオンのときだけ使われます。範囲は 256 から 2048。重いグラフでは 512 を試してください。 |
| **No preview when collapsed** | On | 折りたたまれた FX ノードはプレビューを描画しません。 |
| **Hide FX on-node previews** | Off | すべての LC image FX プレビューを非表示にします。 |
| **Recent colors** | On | 右クリックの **Colors** メニューに、最後に使った8色のカスタムカラーを保持します。Custom Scripts がインストールされていない場合は、Custom ピッカーを追加します。 |
| **Skin Beauty full preview override** | On | half-res や clamp がオンでも **LC Skin Beauty** はフル品質のプレビューを保つので、肌にズームインして確認できます。ワイプは引き続き **Remove wipe** に従います。 |
| **LoRA loader info button** | On | **LC LoRA Loader** の各行に ℹ ボタンを表示します。トリガーワードは LoRA ファイル自体から取得します(インターネット不要)。オフにするとすっきりします。 |
| **Preview distance (px)** | 40 | ノードのテキストと同じように、ノード上の画像は、この値より小さく描画されるほどズームアウトするとオフになります。小さいプレビューから先にオフになります。0 = 常に描画。 |

**影響を受けないもの:** **LC Image Compare 🔎**、**LC Image Split 🖼️**、**LC Dynamic Overlay** は、何があってもフルプレビューとワイプを保ちます(大きくズームアウトしたときだけ **Preview distance** でオフになります)。

**おすすめのセットアップ**
- **通常使い:** すべてデフォルトのままにします。
- **グラフが重いとき:** **Half-resolution previews** と **Clamp longest side**(Max edge 512)をオンにします。**No preview when collapsed** はオンのままにします。
- **キャンバスを最軽量にする:** **Hide FX on-node previews** をオンにします。Before/After を見たいときは **Image Compare** か **Image Split** を使います。
- 💡 変更は次の再描画で反映されます。キャンバスを少しパンするだけで、再起動は不要です。

---

"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"- Yoda Auditore, Assassin's Wars

ko.text:
# LC123 Settings ⚙️

**어디 있나요?** **Settings**(톱니바퀴)를 열고 **LC123 Settings ⚙️**로 가세요. 다섯 개 섹션이 있어요: **Align**, **Connections**, **Notes**, **Optimization**, **Performance**.

- 💡 설정이 안 보이나요? ComfyUI를 재시작한 다음 **Ctrl+F5**를 눌러 브라우저가 새 파일을 불러오게 하세요.

---

### 📐 Align

**Align tool**
- 기본값: **On**
- 도구 전체의 스위치예요. Off = 상단 툴바의 **Align** 버튼(LC 로고)과 아래 기능이 모두 사라져요.
- 켜 두면 **Align** 버튼이 **열려 있는 워크플로우**에 대해 Align을 켜고 끄요: 빨간 불꽃이 있는 밝은 회색 = 켜짐, 회색 불꽃이 있는 어두운 회색 = 꺼짐.
    - 켜짐/꺼짐은 워크플로우에 저장돼요. Align을 켠 채로 저장하면 새 ComfyUI에서도 Align이 켜진 채로 열려요.
    - 워크플로우 탭마다 따로 기억해요. 탭을 바꾸면 도구도 그 탭을 따라가요 (한쪽은 켜짐, 다른 쪽은 꺼짐, 헷갈릴 일 없어요).
    - 켜고 끄는 것도 워크플로우 변경으로 쳐서, 저장 안 됨 표시 점이 떠요.
- 노드는 **Node lines**에, 그룹은 **Group lines**에 스냅돼요. 가까워지면 선이 밝아져요.
- 클래식 캔버스와 **Nodes 2.0**에서 모두 작동해요.
- **Snap distance**는 ComfyUI 자체의 **Snap to grid size**(Settings > Lite Graph > Canvas)예요. 격자가 작을수록 더 촘촘하게 스냅돼요. 새 선도 그 격자에 맞춰져요.
    - 드래그하는 동안 **Shift**를 누르면 드래그가 ComfyUI 자체의 격자 스냅으로 넘어가요 (선 스냅 없음). **Always snap to grid**가 켜져 있어도, 선이 잡은 축에서는 선 스냅이 우선해요.

**Rulers**
- 기본값: **On**
- Align이 켜져 있는 동안 위쪽과 왼쪽 가장자리에 눈금자가 나타나요:
    - 눈금자를 **왼쪽 클릭**: **Node line**(파랑)을 추가해요. 노드가 거기에 스냅돼요.
    - 눈금자를 **오른쪽 클릭**: **Group line**(주황)을 추가해요. 그룹이 거기에 스냅돼요.
    - 선의 마커를 다시 클릭하면 삭제돼요. 마커를 끌면 옮겨요.
- 선은 워크플로우와 함께 저장돼요.

**Line reveal distance (px)**
- 기본값: **120**
- 커서나 끌고 있는 대상이 이 거리까지 가까워질 때까지 선은 보이지 않아요.

**Also snap to other nodes and groups**
- 기본값: **Off**
- On = 다른 노드의 가장자리와 중심에도 스냅돼요 (그쪽은 선이 표시되지 않아요).

---

### 🔌 Connections

**Connection FX**
- 기본값: **Off**
- 선을 끄는 동안, 연결할 수 있는 모든 소켓이 자기 소켓 색으로 빛나요.
- 가까이 가면 소켓에서 링이 퍼져 나와요. 가까울수록 더 크고 밝아요.
- **Connection FX reach (px):** 링이 시작되려면 커서가 얼마나 가까워야 하는지. 기본값 160.
- **Connection FX zoomed-out glow (%):** 줌 아웃하면 유효한 모든 소켓이 더 밝게 빛나서 찾기 쉬워요. 기본값 60.
- 클래식 캔버스 전용이에요. **Nodes 2.0**이 켜져 있으면 작동하지 않아요.

---



---

### 🩺 Optimization

**Optimization report**
- 버튼 하나예요. 캔버스를 몇 초 동안 알아서 이동시키면서, 열려 있는 워크플로우의 모든 팩이 그리고 실행하는 것의 시간을 재고 파일을 스캔해요.
- 캔버스를 느리게 만드는 것의 목록이 큰 순서대로 나오고, 다음처럼 분류돼요:
    - **해당 팩 자체의 설정** (정확한 설정 이름, 위치, 현재 값)
    - **LC123 optimization settings**
    - **ComfyUI settings**
    - **사이드바 탭**
    - **작동에 필요한 것** (설정 없음, 그 팩이 원래 그렇게 작동해요)
- 열려 있는 워크플로우에서 쓰는 노드 팩만 분석해요.
- 제안하는 모든 설정은 현재 값과 대조해서 확인해요:
    - ⚠️ 큰 효과 · ✅ 할 만한 효과 · 💡 작은 효과
    - ⚪ 이미 설정됨 · ➖ 해당 없음 · ℹ️ 필수, 설정 없음
- **Show last run:** 맨 위 버튼으로 이전 리포트로 전환해요. 새로 실행할 때마다 지난번 이후 무엇이 빨라졌고 어떤 수정이 끝났는지도 보여줘요.
    - 마지막 실행만 보관돼요 (새로고침해도 유지). 실행할 때마다 덮어써요.
- 아무것도 바꾸지 않아요. (실행 중에는 마우스를 가만히 두세요.)
- 💡 빈 캔버스를 우클릭한 메뉴에도 있어요.

---

### ⚡ Performance

캔버스에 보이는 것만 바꿔요. 생성, VRAM, **Save Image**, 모든 **IMAGE** 출력은 전체 해상도 그대로예요. (가벼운 미리보기가 가벼운 이미지를 뜻하지는 않아요.)

| 설정 | 기본값 | 기능 |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove wipe** | Off | LC 이미지 FX 노드의 hover A/B 와이프를 꺼요. 마지막 결과는 그대로 보여요. |
| **Half-resolution previews** | Off | FX 미리보기를 절반 크기로 그려요. 캔버스를 움직일 때 부담이 줄어요. |
| **Clamp longest side** | Off | 노드 위 미리보기를 줄여서 가장 긴 변이 **Max edge**에 맞게 해요. |
| **Max edge (px)** | 768 | **Clamp longest side**가 켜져 있을 때만 사용돼요. 범위 256에서 2048. 무거운 그래프에서는 512를 써 보세요. |
| **No preview when collapsed** | On | 접힌 FX 노드는 미리보기를 그리지 않아요. |
| **Hide FX on-node previews** | Off | LC 이미지 FX 미리보기를 전부 숨겨요. |
| **Recent colors** | On | 우클릭 **Colors** 메뉴에 최근 사용한 사용자 색 8개를 보관해요. Custom Scripts가 설치되어 있지 않으면 Custom 선택기를 추가해요. |
| **Skin Beauty full preview override** | On | half-res나 clamp가 켜져 있어도 **LC Skin Beauty**는 전체 품질 미리보기를 유지해서 피부를 확대해서 볼 수 있어요. 와이프는 계속 **Remove wipe**를 따라요. |
| **LoRA loader info button** | On | 각 **LC LoRA Loader** 행에 ℹ 버튼을 표시해요. 트리거 단어는 LoRA 파일 자체에서 가져와요 (인터넷 불필요). 깔끔하게 보려면 끄세요. |
| **Preview distance (px)** | 40 | 노드 텍스트처럼, 노드 위 이미지는 이 값보다 작게 그려질 만큼 줌 아웃하면 꺼져요. 작은 미리보기부터 먼저 꺼져요. 0 = 항상 그림. |

**영향받지 않는 것:** **LC Image Compare 🔎**, **LC Image Split 🖼️**, **LC Dynamic Overlay**는 어떤 설정이든 전체 미리보기와 와이프를 유지해요 (많이 줌 아웃했을 때 **Preview distance**만 이들을 꺼요).

**추천 설정**
- **일반 사용:** 전부 기본값으로 두세요.
- **그래프가 버벅일 때:** **Half-resolution previews**와 **Clamp longest side**(Max edge 512)를 켜세요. **No preview when collapsed**는 켜 두세요.
- **가장 가벼운 캔버스:** **Hide FX on-node previews**를 켜세요. before/after를 봐야 할 때는 **Image Compare**나 **Image Split**을 쓰세요.
- 💡 변경은 다음 redraw 때 적용돼요. 캔버스를 살짝 움직이면 되고, 재시작은 필요 없어요.

---

"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"- Yoda Auditore, Assassin's Wars

# LC123 Settings ⚙️

**Where are they?** Open **Settings** (the gear), then **LC123 Settings ⚙️**. There are five sections: **Align**, **Connections**, **Notes**, **Optimization** and **Performance**.

- 💡 Missing a setting? Restart ComfyUI, then press **Ctrl+F5** so the browser loads the new files.

---

### 📐 Align

**Align tool**
- Default: **On**
- The switch for the whole tool. Off = no **Align** button (the LC logo) in the top toolbar and none of the features below.
- With it on, the **Align** button turns Align on or off **for the open workflow**: light gray with the red flame = on, dark gray with a gray flame = off.
    - That on/off is saved in the workflow. Save it with Align on and it opens with Align on, even on a fresh ComfyUI.
    - Every workflow tab keeps its own. Switch tabs and the tool follows that tab (on in one, off in the other, no mix-ups).
    - Turning it on or off counts as a change to the workflow, so you get the unsaved dot.
- Nodes snap to **Node lines**, groups snap to **Group lines**. A line lights up when you get close.
- Works on the classic canvas and in **Nodes 2.0**.
- **Snap distance** is ComfyUI's own **Snap to grid size** (Settings > Lite Graph > Canvas). Smaller grid = tighter snap. New lines land on that grid too.
    - **Shift** while dragging hands the drag to ComfyUI's own grid snap (no line snap). With **Always snap to grid** on, a line snap still wins on the axis it caught.

**Rulers**
- Default: **On**
- Rulers on the top and left edge while Align is on:
    - **Left click** a ruler: adds a **Node line** (blue). Nodes snap to it.
    - **Right click** a ruler: adds a **Group line** (orange). Groups snap to it.
    - Click a line's marker again to remove it. Drag a marker to move it.
- Lines save with the workflow.

**Line reveal distance (px)**
- Default: **120**
- Lines stay invisible until the cursor or whatever you drag gets this close.

**Also snap to other nodes and groups**
- Default: **Off**
- On = also snap to other nodes' edges and centers (no line is shown for those).

---

### 🔌 Connections

**Connection FX**
- Default: **Off**
- While you drag a wire, every socket it can plug into glows in its socket color.
- Get close and rings pulse out of the socket. Closer = bigger and brighter.
- **Connection FX reach (px):** how close the cursor has to be before the rings start. Default 160.
- **Connection FX zoomed-out glow (%):** zoomed out, every valid socket glows brighter so you can find it. Default 60.
- Classic canvas only. With **Nodes 2.0** on it stays out of the way.

---



---

### 🩺 Optimization

**Optimization report**
- One button. It pans the canvas by itself for a few seconds, times what every pack in the open workflow draws and runs, and scans their files.
- You get a list of what slows your canvas down, biggest first, sorted into:
    - **That pack's own settings** (the exact setting name, where it lives and its current value)
    - **LC123 optimization settings**
    - **ComfyUI settings**
    - **Sidebar tabs**
    - **Required to function** (no setting, it is how that pack works)
- Only node packs used in the open workflow are analyzed.
- Every setting it suggests is checked against its current value:
    - ⚠️ big gain · ✅ worthwhile gain · 💡 small gain
    - ⚪ already set · ➖ does not apply · ℹ️ required, no setting for it
- **Show last run:** the button at the top flips to the previous report. Each new run also shows what got faster and which fixes are done since last time.
    - Only the last run is kept (it survives a refresh). Each run replaces it.
- Nothing is changed. (Keep the mouse still while it runs.)
- 💡 Also in the right-click menu on the empty canvas.

---

### ⚡ Performance

These only change what you see on the canvas. Generation, VRAM, **Save Image** and every **IMAGE** output stay full resolution. (A lighter preview never means a lighter image.)

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove wipe** | Off | Turns off the hover A/B wipe on LC image FX nodes. The last result still shows. |
| **Half-resolution previews** | Off | Draws FX previews at half size. Less work while panning. |
| **Clamp longest side** | Off | Shrinks on-node previews so the longest side fits **Max edge**. |
| **Max edge (px)** | 768 | Only used when **Clamp longest side** is on. Range 256 to 2048. Try 512 on heavy graphs. |
| **No preview when collapsed** | On | Collapsed FX nodes skip drawing their preview. |
| **Hide FX on-node previews** | Off | Hides every LC image FX preview. |
| **Recent colors** | On | Keeps your last 8 custom colors in the right-click **Colors** menu. Adds a Custom picker if Custom Scripts is not installed. |
| **Skin Beauty full preview override** | On | **LC Skin Beauty** keeps a full-quality preview even with half-res or clamp on, so you can still zoom into skin. Wipe still follows **Remove wipe**. |
| **LoRA loader info button** | On | Shows the ℹ button on each **LC LoRA Loader** row. Trigger words come from the LoRA file itself (no internet). Turn off to declutter. |
| **Preview distance (px)** | 40 | Like node text, an on-node image switches off when you zoom out far enough that it is drawn smaller than this. Smaller previews switch off first. 0 = always draw. |

**Never affected:** **LC Image Compare 🔎**, **LC Image Split 🖼️** and **LC Dynamic Overlay** keep their full preview and wipe no matter what (only **Preview distance** switches them off when zoomed far out).

**Suggested setups**
- **Normal use:** leave everything at default.
- **Laggy graph:** turn on **Half-resolution previews** and **Clamp longest side** (Max edge 512). Keep **No preview when collapsed** on.
- **Lightest canvas:** turn on **Hide FX on-node previews**. Use **Image Compare** or **Image Split** when you need to see a before/after.
- 💡 Changes apply on the next redraw. Pan the canvas a little, no restart needed.

---

"True Nothing is. Permitted Everything is"- Yoda Auditore, Assassin's Wars

nodes.title: 🎨 Post Processing

en.text:
# ⚠️🛑 Keep Make🎥 on!

## Post Processing
- ⚠️ This is not automatic
- ⚠️ Don't bypass **Make**: with every shot made it hands over the finished movie
- ⚠️ It will not Save unless turned on💾

**Load Video**
- If you do not load the video, it will not run
- it will automatically load when on

**LC Frame Interpolate 🎞️**
- Doubles the frame rate from 24 to 48 for smoother videos.

**LC RTX Super Resolution ⚡**
- **deblur** sharpens soft edges at the same size. Set **mode** to **upscale** for 2x instead. Lower **strength** if it looks crunchy.
- Under a minute. Needs an NVIDIA RTX card.

**LC Audio Volume 🔊**
- **volume**: 1 = as it is. Below 1 is quieter, above 1 is louder.

**LC Audio EQ 3-Band 🎛️**
- Low, mid and high bands. 0 dB = untouched, so only the bands you move change the sound.
- 💡 A little mid boost (around 1000 Hz) makes voices clearer.

zh.text:
# ⚠️🛑 保持 Make🎥 打开！

## 后期处理
- ⚠️ 这一步不是自动的
- ⚠️ 不要 bypass **Make**：所有镜头都做好时，它会把成片交出来
- ⚠️ 不打开💾就不会保存

**Load Video**
- 不加载视频就不会运行
- 打开时会自动加载

**LC Frame Interpolate 🎞️**
- 把帧率从 24 翻倍到 48，让视频更流畅。

**LC RTX Super Resolution ⚡**
- **deblur** 在同样大小下让发软的边缘更锐利。想要 2x 就把 **mode** 设为 **upscale**。看起来太硬就调低 **strength**。
- 一分钟以内。需要 NVIDIA RTX 显卡。

**LC Audio Volume 🔊**
- **volume**：1 = 原样。低于 1 更小声，高于 1 更大声。

**LC Audio EQ 3-Band 🎛️**
- 低、中、高三段。0 dB = 不改动，只有你调过的频段会改变声音。
- 💡 中频稍微提一点（1000 Hz 左右）人声更清楚。

ja.text:
# ⚠️🛑 Make🎥 はオンのままに！

## Post Processing
- ⚠️ 自動では実行されません
- ⚠️ **Make** をバイパスしないでください：すべてのショットができていれば、完成した映画を渡します
- ⚠️ 💾 をオンにしないと保存されません

**Load Video**
- 動画を読み込まないと動きません
- オンにすると自動で読み込まれます

**LC Frame Interpolate 🎞️**
- フレームレートを 24 から 48 に倍にして、動画を滑らかにします。

**LC RTX Super Resolution ⚡**
- **deblur** は同じサイズのままぼやけたエッジをシャープにします。2x にしたいなら **mode** を **upscale** に。硬すぎるなら **strength** を下げてください。
- 1 分以内。NVIDIA RTX カードが必要です。

**LC Audio Volume 🔊**
- **volume**：1 = そのまま。1 より下で小さく、上で大きくなります。

**LC Audio EQ 3-Band 🎛️**
- 低音・中音・高音の 3 バンド。0 dB = 変化なしなので、動かしたバンドだけ音が変わります。
- 💡 中音（1000 Hz あたり）を少し上げると声がはっきりします。

ko.text:
# ⚠️🛑 Make🎥를 켜 두세요!

## 후처리
- ⚠️ 자동으로 실행되지 않아요
- ⚠️ **Make**를 bypass하지 마세요: 모든 샷이 만들어져 있으면 완성된 영화를 넘겨줘요
- ⚠️ 💾를 켜지 않으면 저장되지 않아요

**Load Video**
- 영상을 불러오지 않으면 실행되지 않아요
- 켜면 자동으로 불러와요

**LC Frame Interpolate 🎞️**
- 프레임레이트를 24에서 48로 두 배로 늘려 영상을 더 부드럽게 만들어요.

**LC RTX Super Resolution ⚡**
- **deblur**는 같은 크기로 흐릿한 가장자리를 선명하게 해요. 2x로 키우려면 **mode**를 **upscale**로 바꾸세요. 너무 딱딱해 보이면 **strength**를 낮추세요.
- 1분 이내. NVIDIA RTX 그래픽카드가 필요해요.

**LC Audio Volume 🔊**
- **volume**: 1 = 그대로. 1보다 낮으면 작게, 높으면 크게.

**LC Audio EQ 3-Band 🎛️**
- 저음, 중음, 고음 3밴드. 0 dB = 그대로라서 움직인 밴드만 소리가 바뀌어요.
- 💡 중음(1000 Hz 근처)을 조금 올리면 목소리가 또렷해져요.
